problems.question: The longest professional tennis match ever played lasted a total of \(11\) hours and \(5\) minutes. How many minutes was this?
hints: Convert the hours to minutes first.
Add the extra \(5\) minutes after multiplying \(11\) by \(60\).
problems.solution: There are \(60\) minutes in an hour, so the total time is \(60 \cdot 11 + 5 = 665\) minutes. Thus, C is the correct answer.

problems.question: In rectangle \(ABCD,\) \(AB=6\) and \(AD=8.\) Point \(M\) is the midpoint of \(\overline{AD}.\) What is the area of \(\triangle AMC?\)
hints: Since \(M\) is the midpoint of \(\overline{AD}\), find \(AM\).
Use \(AM\) as the base and the rectangle’s vertical side length as the height.
problems.solution: Since \(M\) is the midpoint of \(\overline{AD},\) the base \(AM\) has length \(4.\) The altitude from \(C\) to \(\overline{AM}\) has length \(AB=6.\) The area is therefore \(\dfrac{1}{2} \cdot 4 \cdot 6 = 12.\) Thus, A is the correct answer.

problems.question: Four students take an exam. Three of their scores are \(70,\) \(80,\) and \(90.\) If the average of their four scores is \(70,\) then what is the remaining score?
hints: First find the total score needed for an average of \(70\).
Subtract the three known scores from the needed total.
problems.solution: From the average, we can calculate the sum of the scores to be \(4 \cdot 70 = 280.\) This means that the remaining score is \[280 - 70 - 80 - 90 = 40.\] Thus, A is the correct answer.

problems.question: When Cheenu was a boy he could run \(15\) miles in \(3\) hours and \(30\) minutes. As an old man he can now walk \(10\) miles in \(4\) hours. How many minutes longer does it take for him to walk a mile now compared to when he was a boy?
hints: Compare the two paces in minutes per mile.
Convert \(3\) hours \(30\) minutes to minutes before dividing by \(15\).
problems.solution: To better compare the rates, we can change his speed into minutes per mile. As a boy he ran \(15\) miles in \(3 \cdot 60 + 30 = 210\) minutes, which means that he ran at a pace of \(\frac{210}{15} = 14\) minutes per mile. As an adult, he can walk \(10\) miles in \(4 \cdot 60 = 240\) minutes, which means he walks at a pace of \(\frac{240}{10} = 24\) minutes per mile. Subtracting the two, we get that he takes \(10\) more minutes to walk a mile as an adult. Thus, B is the correct answer.

problems.question:
The number \(N\) is a two-digit number with the following properties:
  • When \(N\) is divided by \(9,\) the remainder is \(1.\)
  • When \(N\) is divided by \(10,\) the remainder is \(3.\)
What is the remainder when \(N\) is divided by \(11?\)
hints: The remainder when divided by \(10\) tells you the units digit of \(N\).
List the two-digit numbers ending in \(3\) and test the condition modulo \(9\).
problems.solution: The second condition says that \(N\) ends in \(3\), so the possibilities are \(13,\) \(23,\) \(33,\) \(43,\) \(53,\) \(63,\) \(73,\) \(83,\) \(93.\) Of these, only \(73\) leaves remainder \(1\) when divided by \(9\), because its digit sum is \(10\). Finally, \(73=6\cdot11+7\), so the requested remainder is \(7\). Thus, E is the correct answer.

problems.question: The following bar graph represents the length (in letters) of the names of \(19\) people. What is the median length of these names?
hints: With \(19\) names, the median is the \(10\)th value after sorting.
Count cumulative frequencies from the shortest names upward.
problems.solution: Since there are \(19\) people, each with one corresponding name length, the middle length will be the tenth one. Counting from the left side, the tenth value that we arrive upon is \(4.\) Thus, B is the correct answer.

problems.question: Which of the following numbers is not a perfect square?
hints: Even exponents automatically make perfect squares.
Also remember that a perfect-square base raised to any positive integer power stays a square.
problems.solution: Since any number with an even exponent is a perfect square, we can eliminate A, C, and E. Also, a square number to any power remains a square number, so that rules out D. Thus, B is the correct answer.

problems.question: Find the value of the expression \[ \begin{gathered} 100 - 98 + 96 - 94 + 92 - 90 \\ {}+ \cdots + 8 - 6 + 4 - 2. \end{gathered} \]
hints: Group the expression into pairs of consecutive terms.
Count how many pairs of the form \(n-(n-2)\) appear.
problems.solution: We can group the sum as follows: \[ \begin{gathered} (100 - 98) + (96 - 94) \\ {}+ \cdots + (4 - 2). \end{gathered} \] Note that each pair evaluates to \(2\) and there are \(25\) pairs. Therefore, the total sum is \(2 \cdot 25 = 50.\) Thus, C is the correct answer.

problems.question: What is the sum of the distinct prime integer divisors of \(2016?\)
hints: Factor \(2016\) into primes.
The word “distinct” means to count each prime divisor only once.
problems.solution: We can prime factorize \(2016\) as \(2^5 \cdot 3^2 \cdot 7.\) This shows that the prime divisors of \(2016\) are \(2,\) \(3,\) and \(7.\) The sum of these is \(12,\) so B is the correct answer.

problems.question: Suppose that \(a \ast b\) means \(3a - b.\) What is the value of \(x\) if \[2 \ast (5 \ast x) = 1?\]
hints: Start by simplifying the inner operation \(5\ast x\).
Apply the definition \(a\ast b=3a-b\) twice, from the inside out.
problems.solution: First, \(5\ast x=15-x\). Applying the operation again gives \[\begin{aligned} 2\ast(15-x)&=6-(15-x)\\ &=x-9. \end{aligned}\] Thus \(x-9=1\), so \(x=10\). Thus, D is the correct answer.

problems.question:
Determine how many two-digit numbers satisfy the following property:

When the number is added to the number obtained by reversing its digits, the sum is \(132.\)
hints: Write the two-digit number as \(10a+b\).
Adding the reversed number gives \(11(a+b)\).
problems.solution: Let \(a\) be the tens digit and \(b\) the units digit. Adding the number and its reversal gives \[\begin{aligned} (10a+b)+(10b+a)&=132\\ 11(a+b)&=132, \end{aligned}\] so \(a+b=12\). The valid digit pairs are \((3,9),\) \((4,8),\) \((5,7),\) \((6,6),\) \((7,5),\) \((8,4),\) \((9,3),\) giving \(7\) numbers. Thus, B is the correct answer.

problems.question: Jefferson Middle School has the same number of boys and girls. Three-fourths of the girls and two-thirds of the boys went on a field trip. What fraction of the students on the field trip were girls?
hints: Choose a convenient equal number of boys and girls.
Using \(12\) boys and \(12\) girls makes both fractions whole numbers.
problems.solution: Suppose there are \(12\) girls and \(12\) boys. Then \(9\) girls and \(8\) boys go on the field trip, so the fraction of field-trip students who are girls is \(\dfrac{9}{9+8}=\dfrac9{17}.\) Thus, B is the correct answer.

problems.question: Two different numbers are randomly selected from the set \[\{ - 2, -1, 0, 3, 4, 5\}\] and multiplied together. What is the probability that the product is \(0?\)
hints: A product is \(0\) exactly when one of the selected numbers is \(0\).
Count selections containing \(0\) out of all ways to choose two different numbers.
problems.solution: There are \(\binom62=15\) ways to select two different numbers. A product is \(0\) exactly when one selected number is \(0\), and there are \(5\) choices for the other number. Thus the probability is \(\dfrac5{15}=\dfrac13.\) Thus, D is the correct answer.

problems.question:
Karl’s car uses a gallon of gas every \(35\) miles, and his gas tank holds \(14\) gallons when it is full.

One day, Karl started with a full tank of gas, drove \(350\) miles, bought \(8\) gallons of gas, and continued driving to his destination. When he arrived, his gas tank was half full. How many miles did Karl drive that day?
hints: Track gallons of gas rather than miles at first.
After the \(350\)-mile drive and the refill, compare the new amount of gas to half a tank.
problems.solution: If Karl drove \(350\) miles, then he used \(\frac{350}{35}\) gallons of gas. When he bought more gas, he added \(8\) gallons to \(14 - 10 = 4\) gallons, attaining a total of \(12\) gallons. If his tank was half full when he arrived, he used \(12 - 7 = 5\) gallons, which equates to \(5 \cdot 35 = 175\) miles. Therefore, he traveled a total distance of \(350+175=525\) miles. Thus, A is the correct answer.

problems.question: What is the largest power of \(2\) that is a divisor of \(13^4 - 11^4?\)
hints: Factor \(13^4-11^4\) as a difference of squares.
After factoring, count only the powers of \(2\) in the product.
problems.solution: We can factor this expression using difference of squares. \[\begin{aligned} 13^4-11^4 &=(13^2+11^2)\\ &\qquad\cdot(13^2-11^2)\\ &=290\cdot48\\ &=32\cdot435. \end{aligned}\] Because \(435\) is odd, \(32\) is the largest power of \(2\) that divides the expression. Thus, C is the correct answer.

problems.question: Annie and Bonnie are running laps around a \(400\)-meter oval track. They started together, but Annie has pulled ahead, because she runs \(25\%\) faster than Bonnie. How many laps will Annie have run when she first passes Bonnie?
hints: A \(25\%\) faster pace means Annie runs \(\frac{5}{4}\) as far as Bonnie in the same time.
Annie first passes Bonnie when she has gained one full lap.
problems.solution: Since Annie is \(25\%\) faster than Bonnie, for every lap Bonnie finishes, Annie completes \(1 \dfrac{1}{4}\) laps. Therefore, Annie gains a quarter lap every time Bonnie finishes a lap. With this in mind, for Annie to completely lap Bonnie, Bonnie must finish \(4\) laps, which means that Annie finished \(5\) laps. Thus, D is the correct answer.

problems.question: An ATM password at Fred’s Bank is composed of four digits from \(0\) to \(9,\) with repeated digits allowable. If no password may begin with the sequence \(9,\) \(1,\) \(1,\) then how many passwords are possible?
hints: First count all four-digit passwords when leading zeroes are allowed.
Then subtract the passwords whose first three digits are forced to be \(9,\) \(1,\) \(1\).
problems.solution: The total number of passwords with no conditions is \(10^4.\) The condition removes \(10\) possible passwords since the first \(3\) are determined, and the last one can be anything. Therefore, the number of acceptable passwords is \[10{,}000 - 10 = 9990.\] Thus, D is the correct answer.

problems.question:
In an All-Area track meet, \(216\) sprinters enter a \(100\)-meter dash competition. The track has \(6\) lanes, so only \(6\) sprinters can compete at a time. At the end of each race, the five non-winners are eliminated, and the winner will compete again in a later race.

How many races are needed to determine the champion sprinter?
hints: Think about how many sprinters are eliminated in each race.
To leave one champion from \(216\) sprinters, all but one sprinter must be eliminated.
problems.solution: Note that each race eliminates \(5\) people. For there to be a winner, \(215\) must be eliminated. Therefore, \(\frac{215}{5} = 43\) races are required to eliminate this number of people. Thus, C is the correct answer.

problems.question: The sum of \(25\) consecutive even integers is \(10{,}000.\) What is the largest of these \(25\) consecutive even integers?
hints: For an odd number of consecutive terms, the average is the middle term.
There are \(12\) even integers larger than the middle term.
problems.solution: The average of these numbers is \(\frac{10{,}000}{25} = 400.\) The largest number is \(12\) even numbers away, which means that it equals \(400 + 12 \cdot 2 = 424.\) Thus, E is the correct answer.

problems.question: The least common multiple of \(a\) and \(b\) is \(12,\) and the least common multiple of \(b\) and \(c\) is \(15.\) What is the least possible value of the least common multiple of \(a\) and \(c?\)
hints: Since \(b\) appears in both least common multiples, start with possible values of \(b\).
Try to make \(b\) absorb the common factor \(3\) from \(12\) and \(15\).
problems.solution: We know that \(b\) has to divide both \(12\) and \(15,\) so it must equal either \(1\) or \(3.\) If \(b = 1,\) then \(a = 12\) and \(c = 15,\) making their least common multiple \(60.\) If \(b = 3,\) then we may take \(a = 4\) and \(c = 5.\) The least common multiple in this scenario is \(20.\) Thus, A is the correct answer.

problems.question: A box contains \(3\) red chips and \(2\) green chips. Chips are drawn randomly, one at a time without replacement, until all \(3\) of the reds are drawn or until both green chips are drawn. What is the probability that the \(3\) reds are drawn?
hints: The stopping result is determined by which color appears last in the full ordering of the chips.
Count equally likely positions for the two green chips among the five total chip positions.
problems.solution: The \(3\) reds are drawn before both green chips exactly when a green chip is the last chip in the full ordering. There are \(10\) equally likely ways to choose the two positions of the green chips, and \(4\) of them have a green chip in the last position. Therefore, the desired probability is \[\dfrac{4}{10} = \dfrac{2}{5}.\] Thus, B is the correct answer.

problems.question: Rectangle \(DEFA\) below is a \(3 \times 4\) rectangle with \(DC=CB=BA=1.\) The area of the “bat wings” (shaded area) is
hints: Use the intersection point of the two diagonals that form the bat wings.
Similar triangles give the height of the small triangle cut off at the top.
problems.solution: Define \(I\) to be the midpoint of \(\overline{AD}\) and \(G\) to be the midpoint of \(\overline{EF}.\) Also define \(H\) to be the intersection of \(\overline{CF}\) and \(\overline{BE}.\) The area of \(\triangle BCE\) is \(\dfrac12\cdot1\cdot4=2.\) By symmetry, we can see that \(\triangle BCH\) and \(\triangle EFH\) are similar. Since their bases are in a \(1 : 3\) ratio, so are their altitudes. This means that \(3IH = HG,\) which implies that \(IH = 1.\) Therefore, \([\triangle BCH]=\dfrac12\cdot1\cdot1=\dfrac12.\) It follows that \([\triangle ECH]=2-\dfrac12=\dfrac32.\) Since the figure is symmetric, the total area of the bat wings is \(2\cdot\dfrac32=3.\) Thus, C is the correct answer.

problems.question:
Two congruent circles centered at points \(A\) and \(B\) each pass through the other circle’s center. The line containing both \(A\) and \(B\) is extended to intersect the circles at points \(C\) and \(D.\)

The circles intersect at two points, one of which is \(E.\) What is the degree measure of \(\angle CED?\)
hints: The centers and one intersection point form an equilateral triangle.
Use the fact that angles subtending diameters are right angles.
problems.solution: We know that \(AE = EB = AB\) since they are all radii of congruent circles, so they form an equilateral triangle, which means that \(\angle AEB = 60^{\circ}.\) The segments \(\overline{DB}\) and \(\overline{AC}\) are diameters, so \(\angle DEB=\angle AEC=90^\circ.\) Therefore, \[\begin{aligned} \angle CED &= \angle DEB+\angle AEC\\ &\qquad-\angle AEB\\ &=90^\circ+90^\circ-60^\circ\\ &=120^\circ. \end{aligned}\] Thus, C is the correct answer.

problems.question: The digits \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(4,\) and \(5\) are each used once to write a five-digit number \(PQRST.\) The three-digit number \(PQR\) is divisible by \(4,\) the three-digit number \(QRS\) is divisible by \(5,\) and the three-digit number \(RST\) is divisible by \(3.\) What is \(P?\)
hints: The divisibility by \(5\) condition determines \(S\).
Once \(S\) is known, list the possible two-digit endings \(QR\) that make \(PQR\) divisible by \(4\).
problems.solution: Since \(QRS\) is divisible by \(5,\) we know that \(S = 5.\) Since \(PQR\) is divisible by \(4,\) \(QR\) equals either \(12,\) \(24,\) or \(32.\) If \(QR=12,\) then \(R=2,\) so \(RST=25T\) cannot be divisible by \(3\) using the remaining digits. If \(QR=32,\) then \(R=2\) again, giving the same obstacle. Thus \(QR=24,\) and then \(RST=45T.\) Among the remaining digits, only \(T=3\) makes \(453\) divisible by \(3\). Therefore, \(PQRST = 12453.\) Thus, A is the correct answer.

problems.question: A semicircle is inscribed in an isosceles triangle with base \(16\) and height \(15\) so that the diameter of the semicircle is contained in the base of the triangle as shown. What is the radius of the semicircle?
hints: Draw the radius to the point where the semicircle touches a side of the triangle.
Compare the area of the right half of the triangle using two different bases.
problems.solution: Let \(O\) be the center of the circle, which is the midpoint of \(\overline{AB}.\) We then get that \(BC = 17\) via the Pythagorean theorem. The right half of the isosceles triangle has area \[[\triangle BOC]=\dfrac12\cdot8\cdot15=60.\] The radius \(OE\) is perpendicular to the tangent side \(BC\), so the same area is \(\dfrac12\cdot OE\cdot17.\) Hence \[OE=\dfrac{120}{17}.\] Thus, B is the correct answer.
